# Follow the ideas, not just the LeetCode labels

*Introduction to Algorithms*, fourth edition (Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein; MIT Press, 2022) provides a rigorous progression through algorithm analysis, sorting, data structures, design paradigms, graphs, number theory and string matching.

**This website is not a replacement or reproduction of the textbook.** The knowledge structure is informed by the [publisher's official table of contents](https://mitp-content-server.mit.edu/books/content/sectbyfn/books_pres_0/11599/4e_toc.pdf); all teaching text, numerical examples and code here are original. Some LeetCode tags, such as SQL, Shell, sliding-window heuristics and specific concurrency challenges, are **not standalone chapters in CLRS**.

## Stage I — Understand algorithms and their running time

**CLRS Chapters 1–5:** what an algorithm is, insertion and merge sort, asymptotic notation, divide and conquer, randomisation.

Read [Mathematical Notation](read-the-math.qmd), [Proof and Complexity](prove-and-count.qmd), [Recursion](../recursion/index.qmd), [Divide and Conquer](../divide-and-conquer/index.qmd), [Merge Sort](../merge-sort/index.qmd) and [Randomized](../randomized/index.qmd).

**Target:** be able to explain, with n=8, why a divide-in-half algorithm may have three merge levels, and why a correct algorithm needs an invariant.

## Stage II — Sorting and selection

**CLRS Chapters 6–9:** heaps, quicksort, counting/radix/bucket sorts, selection algorithms.

Read [Sorting](../sorting/index.qmd), [Heap](../heap-priority-queue/index.qmd), [Quickselect](../quickselect/index.qmd), [Counting Sort](../counting-sort/index.qmd), [Bucket Sort](../bucket-sort/index.qmd), [Radix Sort](../radix-sort/index.qmd).

**Target:** explain why general comparison sorting has a lower bound but fixed-range integer sorting may be faster.

## Stage III — Data structures

**CLRS Chapters 10–13:** arrays, linked lists, stacks and queues, hash tables, BSTs and red-black trees.

Read [Array](../array/index.qmd), [Linked List](../linked-list/index.qmd), [Stack](../stack/index.qmd), [Queue](../queue/index.qmd), [Hash Table](../hash-table/index.qmd), [BST](../binary-search-tree/index.qmd).

**Target:** know which invariant makes insertion, deletion, lookup or traversal efficient.

## Stage IV — Problem-solving paradigms

**CLRS Chapters 14–16:** dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, amortised analysis.

Read [Dynamic Programming](../dynamic-programming/index.qmd), [Greedy](../greedy/index.qmd), [Backtracking](../backtracking/index.qmd), [Monotonic Stack](../monotonic-stack/index.qmd) and [Choosing a Pattern](choose-a-pattern.qmd).

**Target:** prove why choosing the earliest-finishing interval is safe, and supply a counterexample to a wrong coin-change greedy rule.

## Stage V — Advanced data and graphs

**CLRS Chapters 17–25:** augmented structures, B-trees, disjoint sets, graph traversal, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths, flows, matching.

Read [Segment Tree](../segment-tree/index.qmd), [Union-Find](../union-find/index.qmd), [BFS](../breadth-first-search/index.qmd), [DFS](../depth-first-search/index.qmd), [Topological Sort](../topological-sort/index.qmd), [MST](../minimum-spanning-tree/index.qmd) and [Shortest Path](../shortest-path/index.qmd).

**Target:** draw a three-vertex graph and show when BFS and Dijkstra disagree.

## Stage VI — Selected topics

**CLRS Chapters 26–35:** parallel and online algorithms, matrices, linear programming, FFT, number theory, string matching, machine-learning algorithms, NP-completeness and approximation.

Read [Data Stream](../data-stream/index.qmd), [Number Theory](../number-theory/index.qmd), [String Matching](../string-matching/index.qmd), [Rolling Hash](../rolling-hash/index.qmd), [Suffix Array](../suffix-array/index.qmd), [Concurrency](../concurrency/index.qmd).

**Target:** understand which assumptions permit a specialised result, and when you need a different algorithm family.

## Topics outside the textbook's direct chapter structure

The LeetCode Problemset tags include interview conveniences and problem domains. [Sliding Window](../sliding-window/index.qmd), [Two Pointers](../two-pointers/index.qmd), [Database](../database/index.qmd), [Shell](../shell/index.qmd) and [Interactive](../interactive/index.qmd) remain valuable, but should not be falsely attributed to named CLRS chapters.

Use the [LeetCode topic catalogue](../index.qmd) for practice, and these textbook stages to understand the **why** behind each technique.

## Your recommended route

Start from [Sliding Window](../sliding-window/index.qmd) → [Prefix Sum](../prefix-sum/index.qmd) → [Binary Search](../binary-search/index.qmd) → [Backtracking](../backtracking/index.qmd) → [Dynamic Programming](../dynamic-programming/index.qmd) → [Greedy](../greedy/index.qmd) → [BFS](../breadth-first-search/index.qmd) → [Shortest Path](../shortest-path/index.qmd).

At each step, explain the formula in plain English, substitute numerical values and derive a proof before running code.
